Nevertheless, these stories possess certain likenesses to truth, which the poets use to build up these very claims, even though they may seem false or even shameful. For every discourse written by the learned Greeks concerning antiquity has two principal authors: **Hesiod** and **Orpheus**, whom they say lived during the time of **Gideon** <note>original: *Gedeonis* — a judge of ancient Israel. Early scholars often tried to align classical mythology with Biblical timelines to create a unified history of the world.</note>. The writings of these men are divided into two levels of understanding: the literal sense and the **allegory** <note>original: *allegoriam* — a story or image that carries a deeper, symbolic meaning beyond the literal words.</note>. 

The crowd of the common people flocked toward the literal meanings. However, the philosophers and the learned—whose eloquence was greatly admired—maintained the allegorical meanings. According to this view, the planets of the heavens and certain stars are called by the names of those who were clearly once mortal men. Indeed, even their tombs and mausoleums are still pointed out in various places today: that of **Saturn** on Mount Caucasus; **Jupiter** <note>original: *Iouis*</note> in Crete; **Mercury** at Hermopolis, a city of Cyprus; **Venus** in Cyprus; **Mars** in Thrace; **Liber** <note>original: *Liberi* — another name for Bacchus or Dionysus.</note> at Thebes, where it is said he was also torn to pieces; and that of **Hercules**,

This is similar to soldiers who, wishing to hide from enemies and conceal themselves, throw away their own shields by which they are usually recognized; in order to remain unknown, they take up the shields of others, and thus elude the hands of the enemy or their treacherous traps.

*Stilbon of Arcadia will change his shield*, that is, the star of Mercury. **Stilbon of Arcadia** <margin>Stilbon</margin> <note>Stilbon is an ancient Greek name for the planet Mercury, meaning "The Gleaming One."</note> was a certain philosopher; in Arcadia there was a man who was most learned in every way. For this reason, Mercury was called Stilbon, due to the similarity of their studies. He flourished in the times of **Moses** and was the grandson of **Atlas**, the brother of **Prometheus**, born of Atlas’s daughter **Maia**. He was the propagator and inventor of many arts. By passing these arts on to men, he earned the right to be considered a God by them after his death, and his seat was placed among the number of the planets.

The name **Mercury** <margin>Mercury</margin> is interpreted as "speech," as if it were "running in the middle" <note>A medieval folk etymology: "Mercurius" was thought to derive from "medius currens."</note>, because speech is a kind of mediator between men. For this reason, he is called **Hermes** in Greek, which means speech or interpretation. He is also said to preside over merchandise <note>The translator links "Mercury" to "merces" (goods/merchandise).</note>, because he runs as a mediator between buyers and sellers. He is depicted as having wings because speech travels swiftly. He is also called the master of theft because speech often deceives the minds of those listening. He holds a rod with which he separates the venom of serpents <note>The Caduceus, Mercury's staff.</note>, because the speech of wisdom pacifies those who are in discord and those who disagree through "serpentine" wickedness. He is also depicted as having a dog-like <note>The text breaks off at "caninū" (canine), likely referring to the "Hermanubis" tradition where Mercury was associated with the dog-headed Egyptian god Anubis.</note>

### THE PROPHECIES OF MERLIN

...according to the voices of the Gospels and the prophets, the brilliance of Mars itself shall also perish, and he shall provide only the horror of night for the earth. There follows: *Iron Orion shall bare his sword; the watery Phoebus shall trouble the clouds.* <note>original: "Nudabit ensem Orion ferreus, vexabit nubes Phœbus æquoreus." Phoebus is a name for the Sun, here described as "watery" or "of the sea."</note> This Orion, whom he mentions here, is not one of the seven planets; but because it is a distinguished constellation, known to almost everyone, and is contained among the signs of the Zodiac—specifically near the "knees" of Taurus—he therefore commemorates it among the planets themselves, saying: *Iron Orion shall bare his sword.* 

First, according to the histories of the Greeks or the songs of the poets, we must see who <margin>Orion.</margin> this Orion was, and why he was so named. They tell us that Orion was a hunter who, because he wished to ravish Diana <note>The Roman goddess of the hunt and chastity.</note>, was killed by her arrows. They say, however, that he was transformed into a constellation, which they call Orion after his name. Furthermore, Orion is said to be named as if he were "Urion," because they claim he was born from the urine of Jove <note>Jupiter, the king of the gods.</note>; and this refers to the flooding of rains. For he "is born" <note>Meaning the constellation rises in the sky.</note> during the winter season, creating tempests and rains. Whence, by an elegant figure of speech, they claim he sprang from the urine of Jove. For they interpret "Jove" as the air; furthermore, all rain happens either from the air or within the air. For above the Moon, there is no storm of rain, no madness of winds, and no crash of lightning, but all things are calm and prepared. Whence Lucan <note>Marcus Annaeus Lucanus (39–65 AD), a Roman poet.</note> says:

> *The air nearer to the earth is ignited by lightning,*
> *And the lowest reaches of the earth receive the winds and the flashing*
> *Streaks of flames; but Olympus rises above the clouds.*

# BOOK VII.

> Behold, the discord of things, diminishing the parts of the Gods,
> Throws them into confusion; the highest realms hold peace;
> Iron Orion shall bare his sword. <note>original: "Ecce Deum minuens rerum discordia partes, / Turbat, summa tenent pacem, / Nudabit ensem Orion ferreus." This verse sets a scene of cosmic upheaval where the lower heavens are in chaos while the highest heavens remain calm.</note>

Orion is not a single star, but a constellation. For this reason, they are sometimes referred to in the plural as the "Orions." However, there are differences between a <margin>Constellation.</margin> **star**, a **constellation**, and **heavenly bodies**. For a "star" <note>original: "stella"</note> is properly called such when it is a single, individual point of light. A "constellation" <note>original: "sydus"</note> truly consists of many stars together, such as the *Pleiades* or the *Hyades*. Regarding these, Virgil wrote: *Arcturus and the rainy Hyades, and the twin Triones*—that is, the two teams of oxen that lead the wagon. <note>Virgil, *Aeneid* 1.744. The "Triones" refer to the stars of the Great and Little Bear (the Big and Little Dippers).</note> Indeed, these oxen are called *triones* as if they were *teriones*, from the word for "threshing" <note>original: "a terendo," to rub or wear down.</note>, because they tread upon the earth. Furthermore, "heavenly bodies" <margin>Heavenly bodies.</margin> <note>original: "astra"</note> are Great Stars, such as *Boötes*. But authors often use these names interchangeably, putting "heavenly bodies" for "stars," and using "stars" indifferently to mean "constellations."

Stars are properly named from "standing" <note>original: "a stando," a common medieval etymology.</note>, because they never leave their fixed places; they do not wander like the planets, nor do they fall, as many people believe. As the Poet says: *And if it did not actually fall, it could have seemed to have fallen.* For those are merely little sparks, not stars, that have slipped down from the ether. This happens when the wind, seeking higher altitudes, drags the ethereal fire along with it; in its path, this fire imitates the appearance of falling stars. As Aemilius says:
> *Often you will also see stars, driven by the wind,*
> *Leaving long trails of white flames behind them.* <note>Likely Aemilius Macer, a Roman poet who wrote on nature and birds.</note>

But let us return to Orion, whom the Latins call "the Watchman," from the act of watching <note>original: "a vigilando," meaning to keep a night watch.</note>, because he is armed with iron and girded with a sword, and is terrible to behold. In short, he is introduced and described as such: *Iron Orion shall bare his sword,* he says, as if threatening the world with imminent destruction. For at that time, he shall be armed...

*The madness of Mercury—that is, the star of Mercury—shall cross its boundaries.* This expression is metaphorical, transferred from the behavior of a living creature to an inanimate object. Indeed, "to rage" or "be mad" is a quality belonging only to living beings. And what wonder is it if the elements are said to be about to rage then, when even the Lord of Sabaoth <note>original: "Dominus Sabaoth," a Hebrew title for God meaning "Lord of Hosts" or "Lord of Armies."</note>—who judges all things with tranquility and in whom no disturbance dwells, nor can dwell—is nevertheless described as "raging" in that final and terrible judgment, so much so that the angels tremble at his fury and, being terrified, are purified. *Jupiter shall leave the permitted paths, and Venus shall desert her appointed lines.* Just as from the beginning of creation the planets and stars have observed the laws appointed for them and certain boundaries to preserve the harmony of nature; so, at the end of the world, to dissolve the structure of the universe—by the will and command of the Lord, whom all things serve—they shall desert those same laws and go beyond their own limits. ### BOOK VII.

...he will cut down mortals with his sickle. Therefore Saturn is said to carry a curved sickle, as I have already said above, because while he is a star harmful due to his coldness, he is much more harmful when in retrograde <note>original: "retrograda." In ancient astrology, a planet appearing to move backward in the sky was often interpreted as being in a state of weakness or malice.</note>. *The twelve-fold number of the houses of the stars shall lament that their guests cross through them so.* By **the twelve-fold number of the houses of the stars**, he means the 12 signs of the Zodiac, which are the houses of the planets and stars. For the planets dwell in these as if in their own houses; they never leave the Zodiac, except for Venus alone, which exceeds it by two degrees. Nor is any part of the earth inhabited except that which lies beneath it <note>The author refers to the medieval geographical theory that only the "climates" or zones of the Earth positioned directly under the celestial Zodiac were temperate enough for human habitation.</note>.

<margin>The Zodiac</margin>
Now, the Zodiac is named from the Greek word *Zoë*, which means "animal" <note>The author is likely thinking of the Greek *zōion* (animal), from which we get "Zodiac" or "circle of animals," though he links it to *zoē* (life).</note>. Indeed, certain of its signs are titled with the names of animals, such as the Ram, the Bull, and so on. The Zodiac ascends from Capricorn, through the Ram, to Cancer. From Cancer, however, it descends through the Scales to Capricorn. You should understand this "ascending" and "descending" according to the position of the lands. This Zodiac is therefore divided into 12 parts by the flow of water, as Macrobius <note>Ambrosius Theodosius Macrobius (c. 400 AD), a Roman author whose writings on cosmology and the "Dream of Scipio" were foundational for medieval science.</note> says. Each part is called a "sign" because in them we mark in which part of the heavens the Sun and other planets are, from where they have departed, and where they ought to return. The arrangement of the signs is as follows, because it is near to us: Cancer, specifically at the boundary of our habitable and torrid zones. Then Leo descends at an angle, followed by Virgo, then Libra <note>original: "libra," meaning the Scales.</note> situated in the middle of the torrid zone. After Libra is Scorpio, then Sagittarius; after which is Capricorn, the most remote from us. Then, obliquely ascending—

> *The Great Bear <note>original: "Ursa"</note> turns the world’s swift courses, never bathed in the deep ocean <note>In the northern hemisphere, the Great Bear (Ursa Major) is circumpolar and never appears to set below the horizon.</note>, and seeing the other stars sink, she desires to dip her flames in the Sea. And because they were the sons of Jupiter, they therefore translated <note>In this context, "translated" means to be moved bodily from earth to heaven</note> them to the celestial realms after death, and assigned two stars to them, which they also called the Twins. Others feel differently about these stars and those twin brothers—namely Castor and Pollux—to whom the stars belong: saying that when one appears, the other sets; and when one sets, the other begins to appear. This they adapt to the twin brothers Castor and Pollux in this way: for they assert that Pollux was immortal, or made so, but Castor was mortal. And so Pollux, for the sake of brotherly love <note>original: "germanae caritatis," referring to the deep affection between siblings</note>, shared his immortality with his brother, participating in his mortality, so that in alternating turns through each year, as one died and went to the underworld, the other would return from the underworld and rise again. <margin>The Scales <note>Libra</note></margin> *The weights of the slanted scales will hang until the ram places his curved horns beneath them.* The Scales <note>Libra</note> is the seventh sign in the zodiac, located in the middle of the torrid zone. without doubt, these are the signs. *The weights of the slanted scales will hang.* And he adds: *Until the ram places his curved horns beneath*, <note>original: "Donec aries recurua cornua sua supponat"</note> understand this to mean beneath the Sun. For just as the Sun, staying in the Scales <note>Libra</note>, creates the autumnal <term>equinox</term> <note>The time of year when day and night are of equal length</note> on the twelfth day before the Kalends of October <note>September 20th</note>, so also when it has entered the Ram <note>Aries</note>, it creates the vernal <note>spring</note> equinox on the twelfth day before the Kalends of April <note>March 21st</note>. <margin>The Ram</margin> Now, the Ram is the sign of the first month. It is called the Ram because of Jupiter Ammon <note>A syncretic god combining the Greek Zeus/Jupiter with the Egyptian Amun, often depicted with ram's horns</note>, whose image the pagans represent with a ram's head and curved horns. They assign the middle line of the world <note>the celestial equator</note> to this sign, just as they do to the Scales. Moreover, the Ram is the sign of the month of March, which not only the Hebrews but also the Romans say is the first month at the beginning of the year. For this reason, they even called it "March" after the name of their progenitor, Mars. Indeed, they assert that the world was created in this month: giving this reason for their claim, that only the springtime is temperate, being both warm and moist. Furthermore, they believe all things are procreated from heat and moisture. Hence their greatest poet, Virgil, speaking of the creation of the world and showing that it was created in the springtime, says among other things: *I could believe that no other days shone at the first birth of the rising world, nor had any other course. <margin>The Crab</margin>
The Crab <note>Cancer</note> is called the fourth sign for this reason: just as that kind of animal moves backwards with retreating steps, so the Sun, when it has come to this sign, being unable to climb any higher, seeks the lower signs again. Then, however, by doing the opposite, it will provoke the Crab, as if to a quarrel against itself. *The Virgin shall climb the back of the Archer, and she shall darken the virgin flowers.* <note>original: "Ascendet virgo dorsum sagittarii, & flores virgineos obfuscabit."</note>

<margin>The Virgin</margin>
The sixth sign of the <term>Zodiac</term> <note>The belt of the heavens through which the sun appears to move</note> is called the Virgin <note>Virgo</note>, because at that time the exhausted earth brings forth no fruits.

<margin>The Archer</margin>
The Archer <note>Sagittarius</note>, moreover, is called the sign of the new month. He is a man deformed with horse-like legs. And because the Archer degenerates in his hind part, it signifies that the Sun at that time is led down from the higher regions to the lower. *The Virgin shall climb the back of the Archer.* Which, according to the literal property of the words, is impossible. For the twelve signs of the Zodiac are twelve equal spaces of the Zodiac itself, separated and divided from one another by the flow of water <note>A reference to ancient water-clocks used to measure the equal "lengths" of the zodiac signs</note>, just as the world is divided into Asia, Africa, and Europe. Therefore, just as Asia cannot pass into Africa or Europe, nor Africa or Europe into Asia, so neither can the Virgin pass into the Archer, or vice versa. Therefore, he used <term>metonymy</term> <note>A figure of speech where the name of one thing is used for another with which it is closely associated</note>, putting the "container" for the "content," saying that the Virgin would climb the back of the Archer—that is, the Sun [moving] from the Virgin...

For it is necessary that the Moon should unfold and run through every sign in a single month that the Sun traverses throughout the circle of a year. But truly now, as the end of the world draws near, when the Sun begins to run through the signs of the Zodiac in a hurry (as we have shown above), as if to accelerate the ruin of the world, while the Moon [remains] in its equal and accustomed space of time, or [separated] from it by 14 days...

# BOOK VII.

it [the moon] wishes to be drawn out through six signs of the <term>Zodiac</term> <note>The "circle of animals," the belt of the heavens divided into twelve signs</note>, and through as many others. In 14 days it will be seen to run back through the other six signs in its chariot—that is, to trouble and disturb the Zodiac with such great speed of running. And this is what he says:

> *The chariot of the Moon shall disturb the Zodiac, and the Pleiades shall break forth into weeping.* <note>original: "Currus Lunæ turbabit Zodiacum, & in fletum prorumpent Pleiades."</note>

By such a figure of speech, this is said in the same way as was mentioned above. The twelve-fold number of the houses of the stars shall weep that their guests pass through in such a manner. <margin>Romans ch. 8 ver. 22.</margin> The Apostle uses such a pattern of speech where he says: *We know that the whole of creation groans and suffers the pains of childbirth until now, etc.* <note>The author uses this biblical reference to explain "personification," where inanimate objects like stars are said to feel emotion.</note> Furthermore, the **Pleiades** are named from the Greek *plistin*, <note>original: "pliſtin," likely referring to pleistos, meaning "most" or "many"</note> that is, from "plurality." For there are seven stars before the knees of the constellation Taurus (the Bull), of which six are visible and one is hidden. The Latins call these the **Virgiliae**, because they rise in the spring. <note>From the Latin "ver" for spring.</note> For by their rising they precede the summer, and by their setting, the winter.

> *The chariot of the Moon shall disturb the Zodiac, and the Pleiades shall break forth into weeping. The duties of Janus shall not return, but with the door closed he shall lie hidden in the borders of Ariadne.*

**Janus** is held among the gods by the pagans; he is fashioned as being "two-faced," as if one who looks both backward and forward, observing the year both as it departs and as it enters. From this, the month of **January** is named, because it is, as it were, the "door" <note>Latin: "ianua"</note> of the world or the heaven, according to the pagans, who want this to be the first month and, in a way, the entrance of the year. Therefore he says: *The duties of Janus shall not return, but with the door closed in the borders*—that is, in the extremities—*Ariadne shall lie hidden.* **Ariadne** was a certain girl, the daughter of a king, to whom after her death they attributed a certain constellation, which is called the **Crown of Ariadne**. <note>Known today as Corona Borealis; the prophecy suggests the normal transition of months and seasons will cease, "hiding" the start of the year within a different constellation.</note>

<image-desc>An ornamental woodcut initial 'G' featuring a classic floral and scrolling vine design.</image-desc> I wish you divine grace and peace, beloved lords and brothers. Although we who follow the camp of Christ <note>original: "Christi castra sectantes"; a common metaphor for the faithful or the clergy as soldiers of Christ.</note> obtain a sufficiently perfect and complete understanding in the Holy Scriptures of those things which it is right for us to know concerning the future, there is nonetheless found among men—of the lowest and most humble, as well as the most noble and highest rank—a great many who consider themselves very wise. They attribute far more to human prophecies or inventions than to divine oracles and true prophecies. This is what especially characterizes this age, notable as it is for its truly wondrous calamities and the detestable persecution of the divine Word.

For there are those who seek out many things from various sources to serve as their consolation; just as we hear daily that Lichtenberger's *Practica* <note>Johannes Lichtenberger (c. 1440–1503) was a famous German astrologer. But because I know for certain from divine oracles that their impious efforts shall be extinguished and even reduced to nothing—even though they do not deign to give credit or even a hearing to this matter—I have therefore [offered] this to them...

-> ### PROPHECIES AND PREDICTIONS <-

...I wished to share this prophecy, to see if perhaps, by listening to seers of their own kind <note>original: "suae farinae"; literally "of their own flour," an idiom meaning people of their own sort or persuasion.</note>, they might desist from their undertaking. For nothing at all should be left untried that seems suitable for healing them and calling them back to the right path; so that if we achieve nothing, we may nonetheless, with a clear conscience and a joyful heart, behold their calamities and destruction, which—as Peter says <note>A reference to 2 Peter 2:3, regarding the judgment of false teachers.</note>—began to approach long ago. 

Now, this present prophecy is presented in pure images <note>original: "meris typis"; Strasder is referring to the famous series of symbolic illustrations known as the *Vaticinia Pontificum* (Prophecies of the Popes), which were often circulated without much accompanying text.</note> without any addition of words; and it most clearly demonstrates what the condition of the Papal kingdom shall be until the very last day of the world, from that time when it began to be reduced to a form of tyranny. 

But lest anyone should think this is a recent fabrication, let all know that I had two copies: one from a **Carthusian** <note>The Carthusians are a silent, contemplative Catholic monastic order; Strasder cites them to provide his source with an air of ancient, monastic authority.</note> monastery, the other from the illustrious library of the **Nuremberg senate**. Neither of these appears so new that anyone seeing them with their own eyes would not freely admit the illustrations are at least a hundred years old. This is something that even those wishing to discredit me can recognize even today. 

Moreover, in one of the books <note>original: "codicum"; referring to manuscript volumes.</note>, it is indicated that the archetype <term>archetype<gloss>the original manuscript from which subsequent copies are made</gloss></term>, from which these two were transcribed two hundred and fifty years ago, was painted specifically in the year **1278**. # OF JOACHIM, THE ABBOT OF CALABRIA,

...lest someone might bring forward another conjecture, some have not hesitated to attribute their own opinions to these pictures. But because it was clear that such writing was more recent than the printed images themselves <note>original: "typis"; referring here to the engraved or printed illustrations in the manuscript or book</note>, and since the older copy had no writing at all attached to it, I have omitted those additions as being plainly foreign to the work. Nevertheless, for the benefit of unlearned and simple people, I have chosen to add an explanation; others, however, who possess even a moderate degree of reason, will perceive what this prophecy means without any explanation at all.

And on this point, let it be up to each individual either to embrace the explanation we have added, or to offer a better one if they are able. Furthermore, I would wish the followers of the **Papal religion** <note>original: "Pontificiae religionis"; a term used by Protestant reformers during this period to distinguish the Roman Catholic Church from their own "reformed" Christianity</note> to be warned here to consider how wretched the state of their affairs is, and to learn how to adapt themselves to the situation. For they must endure this coming ruin, and there is nothing that can turn it aside. They still enjoy the benefit of only one choice: whether they will allow themselves to be moved from their positions peacefully and without heavy loss, or whether they would prefer a hostile overthrow accompanied by the total shipwreck of their fortunes. Certainly, those who commit such a violent deed will not be Christians; nevertheless, God will easily find a **scourge** <note>original: "flagellum"; a common biblical metaphor for a divine instrument of punishment, such as an invading army or a plague</note> to use against them. Regarding this matter, we rely on a much more certain prophecy than even this one—which, by heaven <note>original: "me hercule"; literally "by Hercules," a classical Latin oath used here for emphasis, translated to reflect a strong assertion of truth</note>, is as far from falsehood as can be: May the grace of God always protect us all.

# PROPHECY
## THE FIRST.

In the first prophecy, the Pope is depicted with two bears, into the mouth of one of which he thrusts money. The prophecy as inscribed has it thus: *“Rise up, O bald one <note>original: "Ascende Calue"; an allusion to 2 Kings 2:23, where youths mock the prophet Elisha. In this context, it refers to the tonsured, or shaven, head of the Pope.</note>, so that you may no longer be made bald—you who did not come to shave the bride <note>The "bride" is a traditional metaphor for the Church.</note>, but to nourish the hair of the bear. Go and feed the dove with the purest grains, which are to be trampled by the most evil beast. But beware, lest being deceived by a foolish piety, you offer the infected grains with which you feed the bear to the doves; for if they are infected by the food, they may become gravely ill, to be cured only slowly and with difficulty.”*

Because the Pope boasts greatly of his Apostleship and calls his seat the "Apostolic See," he ought therefore to rightly uphold the duties of the Apostolic office and fulfill all its requirements—as much by preaching and teaching as by consoling and feeding the flock. Meanwhile, however, he should place all hope and trust in the Holy Spirit, so that He might add efficacy to his word and doctrine, and grant him the virtue of suffering—and even of pouring out his life and spirit for its sake, just as the Apostles did. But he turns his ears away from the Holy Spirit and has all his confidence placed in the strength of the bears—that is, in a firm guard of soldiers—just as David, who was most excellent in warlike virtue, is compared to a bear (2 Samuel 17 <note>original: "2.Reg.17." In the Latin Vulgate used at the time, the books of 1 and 2 Samuel were titled as 1 and 2 Kings.</note>). To these soldiers, for this very reason, he bestows coins so that they may defend him strenuously. Thus, from a minister of the divine word, he becomes a political ruler; this denotes the beginning of the papal downfall <note>original: "minae pontificiae"; likely referring to the predicted collapse or the "looming threat" to the Pope's temporal power.</note>.

# PROPHECY
->THE SECOND.<-

In the second prophecy, the Pope stands armed with a cross and thrusts a staff <note>original: "pedum"; a shepherd's crook, symbolizing pastoral authority</note> marked with a Lily into an Eagle. The prophecy inscribed there reads as follows:

> *After the Moon, Mars <note>Mars is the Roman god of war, here symbolizing a period of bloodshed or a specific bellicose leader.</note> shall rise, thirsting for baptismal blood. He shall ascend from the tower to the highest throne, and he shall darken the brightest sun. With the Lily and the cross, he shall torment the Eagle. You shall by no means build a temple for me, for you are a man of blood <note>A biblical allusion to King David, who was forbidden from building the Temple in Jerusalem because he had been a warrior; see 1 Chronicles 22:8.</note> with immoderate zeal, blackening with feigned virtue and scattering superfluities, alone restricting peace, devouring all things.*

Thus, after the Pope began to handle the reins of civil or worldly Empire, and bound himself to the other princes of the earth through mutual treaties, he conquered the Eagle—that is, the Imperial Majesty—and brought it under his yoke by using his cross (his own power) and the Lily, which primarily refers to the aid of the King of France <note>The fleur-de-lis (Lily) was the heraldic symbol of the French monarchy, which often acted as the Papacy's protector against the Holy Roman Emperor (the Eagle).</note>.

# PROPHECY
## THE FOURTH.

In the fourth prophecy: the Pope kneels before a certain hand, behind which is a banner, and a little fox <note>original: "vulpecula"; often a symbol of heresy or craftiness in medieval allegory.</note> grabs his cape.

The prophecy inscribed there reads as follows:

> *Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, a contemplator of all heavenly things, who, led out as a simple man from a dark land, ascends and descends: for a double and foxy voice shall devour his rule, and in tribulation he shall die in a foreign land. Oh, how much the bride <note>The "bride" (sponsa) typically refers to the Church.</note> will grieve over the fall of her lawful groom, handed over to the Lion to be devoured. Why, O entangled man, do you abandon the bride to be given to savage barking dogs? Consider your name, and do your first works so that you may be received in the regions of the East.*

## THE FIFTH.

In the fifth prophecy: the Pope is surrounded on both sides by a certain woman; his right hand also holds a vial <term>vial: a small container, here likely a liturgical chalice or a money vessel</term> full of money, toward which a serpent crawls. The prophecy inscribed there reads as follows:

Alas, alas, imprudent and unjust man, you who are entirely occupied with the shameful nourishment of Venus <note>original: "nutrimentum Veneris"; Venus is used here as a classical metaphor for carnal lust or worldly pleasures.</note>, you do not consider that the land of blessing is to be lost through your part in negligence; hear this along with her, and mourn irremediably: for there shall be a tribulation such as has not been from the beginning.*

# PROPHECY
## THE SIXTH.

In the sixth prophecy, the Pope stands and slits the throat of an Eagle; geese and cocks surround him; there also stands a little monk <term>monachiscus: a diminutive form of 'monk,' often used to denote a figure of lower status or a specific type of friar</term> of a dark color.

He strikes the Cock <note>The Cock (Gallus) traditionally represents the Kingdom of France.</note>, and plucks the Eagle <note>The Eagle (Aquila) represents the Holy Roman Empire.</note>. Why do you so greatly desire the Babylonian sovereignty, which you will not be able to obtain? He will rise up against the just man and bind him in chains.*

The Eagle having now been conquered and gripped by the neck, and also the other birds—namely, the kings—and [the abundance] <note>The text cuts off here, likely continuing with 'abundantia' on the next page.</note> of various riches...

## THE SEVENTH PROPHECY

In the seventh prophecy, a Dragon coiled around a tree speaks with the Pope. 
The prophecy inscribed there reads as follows:

> *This is the blackest bird of the raven kind, destroying the black works of Nero; he will die suddenly in a stony land, when he sees beautiful fruit, sweet to eat; then he will nourish a bud <note>original: "in gemma"; this can mean a jewel, but in a botanical context refers to a bud or sprout.</note> which will provide for him the beginning of death.*

Long ago, the Pope despised divine precepts and mandates, but because a kingdom cannot exist without laws, he devises new laws at the prompting of Satan. Therefore, the devil speaks to him from a thicket, since it is written that God also spoke to Moses in this way: the Pope obeys him and ordains laws of this kind, by which he forbids the use of certain foods and marriage along with other things: although Saint Paul openly asserts this to be a doctrine of Satan in the 4th chapter of 1st Timothy.

## THE EIGHTH PROPHECY

In the eighth prophecy, the Pope sits upon a horse and departs: a certain woman stands before the doors behind the Pope's back.

Indeed, the prophecy inscribed there holds as follows:

> *See here the spouse of the Babylonian woman <note>original: "mulieris Babylonicæ"; a reference to the "Whore of Babylon" from the Book of Revelation, often used by reformers to symbolize a corrupt or apostate Church.</note> fleeing his own bride, leaving her as if widowed and abominable to himself. His name is discordant: cruel, unclean, unjust, lacking in virtue, seeking vanity, immoderately loosening the keys <note>original: "relaxans claues"; a reference to the Power of the Keys (St. Peter's authority), suggesting he is granting indulgences or pardons too freely or for the wrong reasons.</note>, a runner, a gladiator, gathering and corrupting the brightest stars, who will lose his radiance against the dark sun. Finally, the Moon, about to fight, will pursue him; he will fall from on high, and she will darken the lofty places.*

The Pope never undertook anything so absurd that he did not enjoy a happy outcome; whereby it happened that, having neglected the authority of the scriptures and set aside the care and concern for the empire, he indulged in daily pleasures of delight, and also gave himself over entirely to debauchery, feasting, the drunkenness of voices and the harmony of strings, and finally to hunting. Although justice, or piety—expressed here in a female form—earnestly discourages him from these vices and sins, he nevertheless gives no room to her, but rather gazes upon her with grim eyes and a threatening face.

## PROPHECY X.

In the tenth prophecy, the Pope commands the heavens, the Eagle, and the Imperial crown. <note>The "Eagle" is the traditional symbol of the Holy Roman Empire; this illustration depicts the Pope’s claimed supremacy over secular monarchs.</note>
Indeed, the inscribed prophecy holds as follows:

The prophecy indeed ascribed to it holds as follows:

*Let another ascend, favored by a double blessing, a lover of the Crucified, a cultivator of peace, high in intellect; however, what he thinks, he shall not fulfill; high things shall fall, he shall exalt the lowest things; he shall adorn heaven, the groves shall be cut down; stretching out his hands to the poor, he shall betroth widows. And then beware, O rolling and black sphere, lest you be hindered by the North wind <note>original: "vento Aquilonis"; the North wind often symbolizes trials or evil forces in biblical prophecy.</note> in tribulation; defend yourself with the cross.*

The Pope, with all things subjected to his power and established according to his heart's desire, lives like a supreme Monarch, without cares, pains, or fear. Therefore, he casts aside the cross he previously bore, and transfers the wealth and goods of the whole world to his own use. Hence he wears a belt full of <term>ducats</term> <note>Gold coins used as trade currency throughout Europe.</note>; nor does he use the keys according to the rule of the divine word, but the snake—that is, the devil—sustains the duties of governance. This snake strives to overthrow the most precious Gospel through the ruin of most wicked condemnation and persecution, and so to extinguish it entirely. And therefore, the head was cut off from the lamb <note>A symbol of Christ or the innocent Church being sacrificed to worldly power.</note>, and the French kingdom (which this rooster <note>original: "gallinaceus"; a pun on the Latin word "Gallus," which means both "a Gaul/Frenchman" and "a rooster."</note> represents) provides vigorous assistance to the Pope in all these matters.

*...turning, carrying a razor in his hand to cut away superfluities, he shall eat roasted flesh, and drink wine flavored with myrrh; entering as a pauper, considering high things, condescending to the lowest.*

Here, therefore, the Pope insists upon the Imperial crown, and handles it according to his own whim; and the political sword—which the Roman Emperor ought to use for the protection and guardianship of the good, and indeed for the punishment of the wicked—he claims for himself in the same way, and commends it to be handled by ravenous wolves. From this it has come to pass that civil law has consumed the riches of almost the entire world, and yet no one has been able to achieve a final resolution for their legal case. The only reason for this is that the Pope holds in his right hand the "razor of all malice," regarding which Psalm 15 <note>The text cites Psalm 15, but the reference to a tongue like a "sharp razor" is found in Psalm 52 (Psalm 51 in the Latin Vulgate).</note> should be read, where it is clearly taught what this razor is.

## FIFTEENTH PROPHECY

In the fifteenth prophecy, a Salamander—that is, a fierce dragon with a human head, which is encircled by a crown, upon which is also placed a papal cap <note>original: "pileus papalis"; here referring to the ceremonial headgear of the Pope.</note>. The prophecy inscribed there holds thus:

> *This is the final beast, terrible in appearance, which shall pull down the stars. Then the birds shall flee, and only the creeping things shall remain. Cruel beast, consuming all things, hell awaits you.*

But if so great an attack is made against the Pope by the fiery sword of the Holy Spirit—that is, by the word of God which He commanded to be preached, sent down by the glowing tongues of the heavenly spirit—it becomes manifest that the Pope's empire is that beast which, dragging a third part of the stars with its tail, enters into eternal damnation. Revelation 12 and 17. <note>original: "Apoc. 12. & 17."; these chapters of the Apocalypse describe the Great Red Dragon and the Beast that rose from the sea.</note> Indeed, it presents a face that is not unrefined <note>original: "haud illiberalem"; meaning the beast appears noble or dignified at first glance.</note>; but from behind, fraudulently, cunningly, and secretly, it seizes the sword with its teeth in such a way that it is unwilling to abstain even from the pouring of blood from its mouth.

## SIXTEENTH PROPHECY

In the sixteenth prophecy, the Pope is surrounded by bears; one looms over his head, while the remaining two flank him on either side.

->The inscribed prophecy itself reads as follows:<-

> *A wicked breed, a she-bear feeding her cubs, and in five ways <note>original: "in quinq;"</note> disturbing the scepter of Rome with new things, and for thirty-six years it shall walk miserably; it is the beginning of the end of the sect having five sons, for the manner is determined by the figure. The airy city <note>original: "Aerea quoq; ciuitas"; likely referring to Rome or a high-reaching city.</note> shall likewise receive the barbarians. When, however, you see the bear, the mother of dogs, mourn miserably in the height of heaven, so that you may obtain help from God. Most wickedly you shall deceive many under a foreign skin, for once changed, you turn a deceitful gaze while hiding in the earth and practicing deception among many.*

The Pope notices that he is not safe under the protection of Holy Scripture, since it is entirely opposed to him; therefore, with the volume closed, he surrounds himself on all sides with the protection of bears. Both from above and below, from the front and from his shoulders, he hands himself over to be guarded; that is, he commits himself to the protection of soldiers and strives to defend his cause with hostile violence.

### TWENTIETH PROPHECY

Moreover, every rule that you have consumed with the sword in the temples of idols you shall revive after a little while; for three years in the world you, a very old man, will have strength, but you will collapse at the very bottom between two tribulations in the middle.*

In order that it may be understood who that Monk is, he is depicted here in his own garments, holding his sign—namely, a rose—in his hand; I certainly judge him to be Martin Luther. Because in the 40th chapter of Isaiah it says: *All flesh is like grass* <note>Isaiah 40:6; original: "Omnem carnem graminis instar esse"</note>, for that reason he holds a scythe, with which he mows down not indeed grass and herbs, but flesh and whatever is carnal. ## TWENTY-FIRST PROPHECY

In the twenty-first prophecy, a veil is seen, behind which are an Emperor and Empress; before it stands a Pope, and at his feet is a bull.

You alone shall be exalted by glory, and you shall leave the powers most powerfully to the dead, for you shall find it well, like a shower.*

This bull <note>Latin: "taurus"</note> designates the wretched and miserable common people, who have learned from the reading of the divine word that they are burdened by the Pope with intolerable laws of conscience, and by taxes that are by no means to be endured—namely, the constant [extortion] of money <meta>catchword: "ex-" likely leading to "exactionibus" (exactions/taxes) or "extorsionibus" (extortions)</meta>

### TWENTY-THIRD PROPHECY.

In the twenty-third prophecy, there is a city which raises two banners upon two towers, and a great cavalry approaches it.

->The inscribed prophecy reads as follows:<-

> *Alas, alas, wretched city, enduring sorrows and sufferings. For the city, so that the light may appear miserable, shall soon hold arms for a short time. There shall be slaughters within you and the shedding of blood. Whence, beginning from one, they shall not fail in five princedoms from your Monarchy. Dragons shall break the eggs. Those things which they ate as food, they shall tear limb from limb, piece by piece <note>original: "frustatim laniabunt"; to tear into bits</note>, and having been stirred to internal war, an innumerable multitude shall fall by the sword, numbered at six or seven thousand; and every city shall be multiplied in fornication, and the stained man, the adulterer, the plunderer, and the unjust man shall yield. The Sodomite shall see the final light before the eyes of his M.* <note>The letter "M" in such prophecies often refers to a specific title, a name, or even "Mors" (Death).</note>

Since the deadly fury of the people was sharpened daily, and thereafter greater intolerance arose, a remedy was finally sought, and an assembly of all the orders <note>The "orders" or "estates" refers to the social classes of the Holy Roman Empire: the clergy, the nobility, and the commoners.</note> was summoned at Worms <note>original: "VVormatiæ"; referring to the Diet of Worms, a formal deliberative assembly.</note>. Truly, because the divine word was forced there to yield to human judgment, and the sentence was passed not against the Pope, but in his favor, the city was filled with equestrian forces <note>cavalry or knights</note> who exercised supreme power there. And because the Pope's cause was pronounced just and ratified there, his banners are seen flying, raised everywhere.

### TWENTY-FOURTH PROPHECY.

In the twenty-fourth Prophecy, a Pope and a fox are shown; the fox carries the Pope’s banner and keys in its mouth, while another banner is fixed to the Pope’s back.
->The prophecy inscribed there says:<-

> *You have fashioned a fox-like friendship <note>original: "Vulpinam figurasti amicitiam"</note>, patiently restraining your senses like a very old man, possessing the wisdom of age <note>original: "canum habens sensum"; likely referring to the gray hair of old age and the wisdom associated with it.</note>. While pleasures came twofold, you dismissed pleasure sevenfold to be shattered against one another and poured out into the shedding of the valley of blood. You have stretched out your hands for victory. Well and gloriously have you received the prize <term>brauium<gloss>A reward or prize given to the winner of a contest; a term often used in the Vulgate Bible for the "prize" of eternal life.</gloss></term> at the end of your scepter.*

While these things occur, the little fox (that is, the Pope’s own courtiers) carries off his keys and banners. This happens in two ways. Some defend the Pope so foolishly and stupidly that his power appears far weaker through their efforts than it does through his adversaries. Such men include: Sylvester <note>Sylvester Prierias, a Dominican who was the first to systematically oppose Luther.</note>, Radinus, Catharinus, Eck <note>Johann Eck, the primary theological opponent of Martin Luther during the early Reformation.</note>, Emser, Alveld, Fabri, Cochlaeus <note>Johannes Cochlaeus, a prolific and fierce literary opponent of the Protestant Reformation.</note>, and others. However, some do this intentionally because they see that the Pope can no longer remain standing; these people I prefer to pass over in silence.

### TWENTY-FIFTH PROPHECY.

In the twenty-fifth Prophecy, a certain city is again depicted.
->The prophecy inscribed there says:<-

> *Woe to you, city of seven hills <note>A traditional reference to Rome, the city built on seven hills.</note>, when the letter K shall be praised within your walls. Then your downfall shall approach, along with the destruction of your powerful men and those who support injustice. He who has hooked fingers, who is the sickle of desolation <note>original: "falx desertitudinis"</note>,*

<page-num>321</page-num>

...and in the heights, he blasphemed me. Q. V. R. G. <note>These initials likely refer to cryptic prophetic identifiers common in Joachimite literature.</note> And in C. V. T. Enough of the cup of falling blood. John of good grace, Constantine the poor, you should see, you who consider holy things and carry holy items upon your shoulder, lest your dust become a reproach, and a deep beard will be justly cut; and you yourself, the counselor at the death of the Pope <note>original: "consiliarius in morte Pontificis"</note>, whose name is Io. Obi. <note>Possibly a name abbreviation or "Jo[hn] died" (obiit).</note>, will be greatly disgraced.

The decree made at the Diet of Worms <note>The Diet of Worms (1521) was an imperial assembly of the Holy Roman Empire, famous for the Edict of Worms which addressed Martin Luther and the Protestant Reformation.</note> was too weak to resist heavenly teachings; for that reason, a second and then a third assembly was held at Nuremberg <note>original: "Norinbergae"</note>. Here, as is evident from the records, the eternal word of God reigned rather than human dreams. Therefore, neither cavalry troops nor Papal banners are seen here, but rather several severed hands, which Johann Thomas of Habsburg <note>Iohannes Thomas Habspergensis</note> ordered to be cut off from several people around the time of these assemblies. He sent them to Nuremberg to show his contempt for the Imperial government and to demonstrate this wicked deed.

### TWENTY-SIXTH PROPHECY.

In the twenty-sixth prophecy, a naked priest is sitting, and a certain peasant stands near him; at their feet is a small money chest.
The prophecy inscribed there states:

> *And the anointed one <note>original: "vnctus"</note> shall be raised up, who has the nickname of a Monk living on a rock <note>original: "pronomen Monachi petram habitans"</note>. He comes to me from outside, leaving foreign things in mourning, and he leaves behind the wild sustenance of the grape; dead and groaning, gathering goods but scattering every reward of iniquity. He who is entirely justified, when the Black Star appears, then you shall be naked. Likewise, deep in the interior of the earth.*

<header>PROPHECIES AND PREDICTIONS</header>

Thus far we have been able to prophesy without difficulty, since we have seen everything with our own eyes. But now, lest we go astray, may divine grace be with us, because the matter now begins to grow serious. For the Pope shall be deprived of his former majesty, dignity, and wealth; he shall be stripped of pleasure and joy. He will be left naked of all protection from friends; he will be cast down from his money chest; he will lose his purse. Finally, he will be so lacking in all human help and consolation that he will find himself both alone and naked in the deepest anxiety, and he will lie in a pitiable manner in filth and mourning. (Perhaps his limbs and skin will be cared for more softly and elegantly; but I would find that hard to believe.) <note>The author uses irony here, suggesting that despite the Pope's usual luxuries, his spiritual and political fall will leave him truly wretched.</note> Indeed, even this poor peasant <note>referring to the figure in the previous prophecy's illustration</note> will hold him in derision and receive him with mockery. In this, it will find its fulfillment, as you can read what is written in the 18th chapter of the Apocalypse <note>original: "18. Apoca."; referring to the Book of Revelation 18, which describes the fall of Babylon, a passage often used by reformers to symbolize the fall of Rome.</note>.

### TWENTY-SEVENTH PROPHECY.

In the twenty-seventh prophecy, the Pope stands and gives the hat taken from his head to the sheep lying at his feet.

The inscription of the prophecy reads as follows:

> *Dead, and now of forgotten appearance, many know him; although no one sees him, revealed by the Deity, he shall unexpectedly hold the scepters of this empire. For at the same time, an invisible herald revealed in heaven will cry out three times with a great voice: Go with haste to the West of the seven hills <note>The "seven hills" is a traditional reference to the city of Rome.</note>; you will find a man dwelling there, my friend; bring this man to the Royal seats—bald, mild, gentle, of high mind, and sharp...*

*...especially for seeing the future. Within yourself, you shall hold the empire of the seven hills.* <note>original: "In te habebis septem collis imperium"; a reference to Rome, famously built upon seven hills.</note>

Nor will this calamity end suddenly like a passing storm, but it shall be lasting and constant, until at length the Pope confesses that he was not the master of the little sheep, but an unworthy servant (as his ancient title sounds: *Servant of the servants of God* <note>original: "Servus servorum Dei"</note>). He must admit that God alone, through His holy word, presides over and governs the **Christian Commonwealth** <term>Christian Commonwealth: originally "Respublica Christiana," referring to the collective body of the Christian world</term>; which, nevertheless, is far more powerful and excellent than the Pope himself. Wherefore he himself here takes off his crown and restores it to the little sheep. Nor should anyone allow themselves to be terrified, even if the outcome of the matter seems otherwise. For this path must be traveled even if the whole world—and indeed the devil himself—is unwilling, even if this present prophecy did not exist.

## TWENTY-EIGHTH PROPHECY.

IN the twenty-eighth prophecy, a priest is seen, upon whose head a certain angel places the papal crown.

> *Behold likewise a man from the first hidden kind, entering the first, unique for numerous years. He comes naked from the dark rock, so that he may begin a second, shining life. The truest image of the second life, so solidly solid, he shall enter the rock dead after doubled years.* <note>The Latin text here is intentionally cryptic and mystical, using "the rock" as a metaphor for spiritual stability or perhaps a monastic origin.</note>

Once those things are completed, God Himself from heaven will set certain men over the office of **Apostle** <term>Apostle: here meaning a divinely appointed messenger or reformer in the spirit of the original twelve</term>; yet it is not as if in heaven

### PROPHECY XXIX.

IN the twenty-ninth prophecy, the Pope sits upon a throne, and angels hold a canopy <note>original: "aulæum," referring to a ceremonial curtain or backdrop often used to denote status or sanctity.</note>.

->The ascribed prophecy reads as follows:<-

> *Accept the pure tiara <term>tiara: the ceremonial headdress of the Pope, often called a "cidaris" in Latin, symbolizing his spiritual authority</term> entrusted to you and clothe yourself in new garments, though you are an old man in wisdom. Great priest of God, do not be sluggish, but receive it. Think most powerfully upon the end, and guide the scepter-bearer <note>original: "sceptrigeram"; likely referring to the Church or the Papal office itself as a wielder of authority</note> toward the good, fearing nothing else. For you have received this time from above, completed by only three dawns of a circling year and eleven of the stars. To one final end, you have left that which you wondered at, now consecrated. Applaud, for you have calmed the dispute; follow your calling; you have arrived well at your present glory. The Beginning, however, has spoken: You have well-tilled the overturned land; walk toward the heavenly dwellings, for the heavenly beginning and end reside there.*

For if such ministers of the divine word should emerge, their honor and respect will be granted to them once more. For they will be the kind of men about whom Christ said, "He who receives you, receives me, and he who despises you, despises me." <note>A reference to Matthew 10:40 and Luke 10:16.</note>

<page-num>325</page-num>
# THE ABBOT JOACHIM OF CALABRIA

You have found a good life through a lack of worldly glory <note>original: "ingloriatione," suggesting a life of humility or one spent away from the vanities of public fame</note>, and you have received more from virtue than from fortune, yet you shall by no means gain a reward of virtuous grace. For envy will bring about judgments that are harmful to you, though you shall not be deprived of your lot from above. Woe to the city of blood, entirely full of the tearing apart of lies; robbery shall not depart from you—the sound of the whip, the sound of the wheel's rush, and the neighing horse <note>This passage heavily quotes Nahum 3:1-2, describing the downfall of a corrupt city, likely used here as a metaphor for a corrupt ecclesiastical or worldly power</note>. Let the heart of a wild beast be given to him, and let seven times be changed over him <note>A reference to the punishment of Nebuchadnezzar in Daniel 4:16, symbolizing a loss of reason or a period of divine trial</note>. Let his heart be changed from abomination (or from its dwelling place) <gloss>habitatione</gloss>.

This holy state of the Church will endure until the coming of Christ, who in Revelation 5 <note>original: "Apoc. 5"</note> is called the Lamb bearing seven horns. To Him, these ministers of the divine word will commit their crown—that is, their office—and they will restore the power handed down to them, having given an account of the gain which they acquired with the money left to them by the departing Christ <note>A reference to the Parable of the Talents (Matthew 25), where servants must account for the spiritual "wealth" or "talents" they managed in their master's absence</note>. And thus Christ will receive all earthly power and will commend it to His Father: with whom He Himself and we shall reign forever. 

->Which may God, in His mercy,<-
->deign to grant us as soon as possible. Amen.<-
